ground_truth_root_cause: The upstream DNS zone for api.exchangerates.internal was updated by the currency exchange rate API provider, replacing the A record (previously resolving to 203.0.113.42) without an adequate TTL propagation window. The original TTL of 86400s meant the payment-service DNS resolver cached the now-invalid A record 203.0.113.42. When the stale cache expired around 13:54 UTC, all subsequent DNS queries for api.exchangerates.internal returned NXDOMAIN from the authoritative nameserver ns1.exchangerates.internal. The payment-service fell back to the stale cached IP, which was no longer routable, causing all forex lookups to time out. USD-to-USD payments succeeded normally, confirming the failure was strictly scoped to DNS resolution of the forex API. This DNS misconfiguration predates all recent deploys and is entirely unrelated to them.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately: Override the local DNS cache on payment-service pods by manually adding a temporary /etc/hosts entry or DNS override for api.exchangerates.internal pointing to the correct new IP obtained from the exchange rate API provider support team. 2. Re-open the forex circuit breaker once DNS resolves correctly to restore payment processing. 3. Contact the exchange rate API provider to confirm the new A record and verify TTL is set to a low value (300s or less) during future zone migrations. 4. Long-term: Implement DNS-level health checks and alerting on NXDOMAIN responses for critical upstream dependencies; consider adding a static fallback IP or secondary DNS resolver for the forex API.
red_herring: The most recent feature-bearing deploy (sha=9f3e1a7b2d84c05f6, 13:25 UTC) rolled out an ML recommendation algorithm touching model serving configuration files, landing approximately 35 minutes before the incident alert fired at 14:06 UTC. This looks causally suspicious: the changed files include recommendation serving logic and flag routing code that runs inline with payment processing, and the 20% cohort rollout coincides temporally with the degradation window. However, multiple log lines in the log_window directly exculpate this deploy: (a) at 14:04:20Z the service logs that the ML recommendation flag cohort latency is p50=18ms p99=34ms within normal bounds; (b) at 14:05:11Z the service logs that USD-only payments with no forex are completing successfully at p99=210ms, confirming the ML flag is NOT contributing to failures; (c) at 14:06:01Z the incident context log explicitly notes recommendation flag healthy with no errors in ML serving layer; and (d) all successful payments in the log are USD-to-USD with no forex required, while all failures are strictly NXDOMAIN and timeout class errors against api.exchangerates.internal, a pattern inconsistent with any ML model serving regression. Furthermore, the DNS NXDOMAIN condition is logged as beginning at approximately 13:54 UTC, six minutes before the suspicious deploy was even completed.
